# Codex Tray Indicator v1.3.0

First public open-source release, licensed under MIT.

## What it does

- Shows Codex CLI lifecycle state in the Windows notification area: Inactive,
  Ready, Busy, and Error, with optional completion notifications.
- Integrates Codex hooks with one selected WSL distribution. Review `/hooks`
  and choose Trust yourself; setup never bypasses this required approval.
- Supports per-user installation, Windows startup, and a portable executable.
- Optionally mirrors the indicator on a supported Turing 3.5-inch Revision A
  USB display. Other protocols or display revisions are not supported.
- Does not display or retain prompt or response text.

This release tracks Codex CLI **in WSL only**. It does not track native Windows
Codex CLI or the Codex desktop app, and does not combine multiple WSL distributions.

## Downloads and setup

The release contains exactly these three files:

- `CodexTraySetup.exe` — recommended per-user Windows x64 installer.
- `CodexTray.exe` — portable Windows x64 application.
- `SHA256SUMS.txt` — SHA-256 hashes for both executables.

The executables include the .NET runtime; end users do not need a separate .NET SDK.
Windows, WSL, and Codex CLI requirements and complete configuration steps are in
the [English README](../../blob/v1.3.0/README.md#installation) and
[Ukrainian README](../../blob/v1.3.0/README.uk.md#installation).

Download the executable and checksum manifest from this same release, then
[verify the SHA-256 hashes](../../blob/v1.3.0/README.md#checksums) **before running**.
Stop if a hash does not match. Matching hashes detect corruption or mismatched
files; they do not independently authenticate the publisher if the release
account or manifest is compromised.

## Unsigned release warning

v1.3.0 has **no Authenticode signature**. Windows may show **Unknown Publisher**,
and SmartScreen may warn about an unrecognized application. A matching hash does
not remove those warnings or make a download inherently trusted.

Do not disable antivirus, SmartScreen, organizational security policy, or Codex
hook-trust controls. If your policy blocks unsigned applications, do not run
this release; review/build the source where permitted or wait for a signed release.

## Maintainer acceptance

Tag automation creates only an **unpublished draft**. Hosted checks exclude real
WSL integration and USB hardware tests. Passing those checks does not replace
full local tests, clean installer acceptance, hook Trust, notifications, autostart,
reinstall/uninstall checks, and supported-device testing. The owner must review
the draft and verify downloaded hashes before explicitly approving publication.
